problem_statement:
uptimeStrip (and heatStrip) merge narrow ticks into one solid bar

When a strip has many periods, the ticks run together. For example, 84 two-hour periods in a 336px uptimeStrip give each tick 4px, and every tick is drawn the full 4px wide, so the strip reads as one continuous bar instead of 84 separate periods. A gap between ticks only appears once a tick is wider than 4px. heatStrip has the same problem.

Reproduce:

```ts
uptimeStrip({ slots: Array(84).fill("up"), label: "x", width: 336 });
```

Every `<rect>` has `width="4"`, so neighbouring ticks touch.

Expected: narrow ticks should still keep a visible gap between them:
- a tick with 3px or more of space keeps a 1px gap (84 periods in 336px should draw 3px-wide ticks; 100 periods in 250px should draw 2px-wide ticks)
- a tick with 2px up to 3px of space keeps a half-pixel gap (100 periods in 150px should draw 1.5px-wide ticks)
- only ticks narrower than 2px may touch.

Related visual issue in the same release: area charts fill their bands at 0.85 opacity, which hides the gridlines and makes a stack read as one solid block. The bands should be much lighter (around 0.3), with a 2px line along each band's top edge so the shape still reads. This should apply to both the Observable Plot area chart and the lite area chart.
fail_to_pass: npx vitest run test/primitives.test.ts -t "keeps a gap between narrow ticks"
pass_to_pass: npx vitest run test/primitives.test.ts -t "encodes status by height as well as color"
npx vitest run test/primitives.test.ts -t "uses per-slot labels in hover details"
